articles.title: HBO’s Welcome to Derry series just ain’t it
articles.summary: HBO’s It: Welcome to Derry — out November 26th — can’t build enough suspense for potent scares.
articles.body: You’ve never had to wait all that long for Hollywood to adapt another one of Stephen King’s tales, but the past couple of years have felt unusually flush with films and series based on the prolific author’s work. Some of the recent projects, like Carrie, Children of the Corn, and ’Salem’s Lot were duds that couldn’t re-create the terrifying magic that made earlier adaptations of those stories horror classics. But others, like The Life of Chuck and The Long Walk, were (for the most part) critical hits that reminded audiences how powerful King’s narratives could be in the right filmmakers’ hands. This new wave of King adaptations was jumpstarted by Warner Bros. Discovery’s pair of relatively recent It features that did a tremendous job of making the classic story of kids battling an eldritch monster feel fresh. HBO’s new It: Welcome to Derry prequel series has potential; you can almost see how an It prequel digging into Pennywise’s past could make for a fascinating expansion on this chunk of King’s oeuvre. But rather than fleshing out Derry’s history with exciting and disturbing new details, the show mostly rehashes the original It’s beats with a lower production budget that makes everything feel too chintzy to be scary. This might not be such a huge issue if Welcome to Derry’s story were more engaging, if its performances were stronger, or if its moments of horror were actually scary. But the most alarming thing about this show is how long it takes for the killer clown to show up and get down to business. Set a few decades before the events of It, Welcome to Derry zooms in on the fictional Maine town during the thick of the Civil Rights Movement. In 1962, life in Derry is as quiet as it is simple for the city’s overwhelmingly white population. Nuclear families are the norm and no one really thinks to wonder why the military has recently spun up a secretive base nearby. [Media: Though Derry’s population of Indigenous people has long since been displaced, it’s easy for white residents to convince themselves that racism doesn’t exist in the town because local projectionist Hank Grogan (Stephen Rider) is a Black man. It’s also easy for many of Derry’s residents to forget how many children have disappeared under mysterious and inexplicable circumstances over the years. But when a young boy vanishes after leaving the movie theater one evening, the people of Derry are quick to place blame on Hank and assume that he’s done something nefarious to the kid. Other local kids, like Hank’s daughter Ronnie (Amanda Christine) and her classmate Lilly (Clara Stack), know that the accused man is innocent. But they also know that no one will believe them if they try to explain the otherworldly presence they have identified as the real danger. After Welcome to Derry first gives you a glimpse of one of the many forms Pennywise (Bill Skarsgård, who also executive produces) takes on to scare people, it becomes very clear that showrunners Jason Fuchs and Brad Caleb Kane are not all that interested in telling a story that feels materially different from the original It’s. Each of the show’s young characters has unnerving encounters with the monster long before they learn its name, what it wants, or how it loves to kill kids. Being hunted by Pennywise is new to all of them, but if you’ve read King’s novel or seen any of its adaptations, you can easily see how many of Welcome to Derry’s beats are cribbed from the recent It movies. The monster whispers to the kids from bathroom sinks and pops up around town disguised as adults who appear normal until they start smiling with deranged expressions on their faces. What does feel a bit distinct here is the way Pennywise actually manages to kill quite a few people who initially seem poised to become Welcome to Derry’s central characters. But those surprises quickly give way to a by-the-numbers plot that feels overly concerned with spelling out what’s going on in exhaustive detail. The show struggles to maintain any real sense of suspense as it shifts focus between its proto-Losers Club and adult characters like Air Force Major Leroy Hanlon (Jovan Adepo), his wife Charlotte (Taylour Paige), and General Shaw (James Remar). As transplants new to Derry, all of them can sense that there is something deeply strange about the town and the way long-term residents tend to behave toward outsiders. You can feel the show trying to use its historical setting to explore the ways in which Pennywise’s presence could make life uniquely dangerous for people of color unlucky enough to wind up living in Derry. [Image: At times, that framing (and a handful of references to DC’s comics) makes it seem like HBO intended for Welcome to Derry to unfold similarly to its Watchmen series. But compared to Watchmen, this prequel’s social commentary regarding racism is relatively thin, and it begins to feel somewhat hollow once the show starts trying to riff on some of the tropes that shaped King’s Pet Sematary. As Welcome to Derry introduces supporting characters like a younger version of The Shining’s psychic chef Dick Hallorann (Chris Chalk), and name-drops locations like the Shawshank prison, you get the sense that HBO might see the series as the beginning of a new franchise. Those details have a way of making the show feel like a testing ground for an interconnected universe of King adaptations. It would all be much more interesting if Welcome to Derry didn’t share so much of its narrative DNA with Stranger Things and if the show’s horror set pieces were a bit more visually inspired. But more often than not, the series’ scares feel rushed out of necessity and the skew more gory than truly frightening, and it is sometimes hard to get a sense of who Welcome to Derry’s target audience is. By the time that Pennywise shows up in his signature clown guise, Welcome to Derry has already long since telegraphed how it’s all going to end and exhausted its ability to conjure up anything that might genuinely take you by surprise. What the show needs is a proper mystery and more character arcs that don’t immediately telegraph how doomed Derry’s residents are fated to be until a new group of intrepid monster slayers show up a few years down the line. But in its first season, Welcome to Derry just doesn’t have what it takes to tell a story you can really sink your teeth into. It: Welcome to Derry also stars Madeleine Stowe, Rudy Mancuso, Mikkal Karim-Fidler, Kimberly Norris Guerrero, Joshua Odjick, and Morningstar Angeline. The series premieres on October 26th.

articles.title: Jenny McCarthy reveals shocking living situation after moving out of California home
articles.summary: Jenny McCarthy opened up about her harrowing health journey on Thursday, revealing that she moved into a tent outside her house after being diagnosed with my...
articles.body:
Jenny McCarthy opened up about her harrowing health journey on Thursday, revealing that she moved into a tent outside her house after being diagnosed with mycotoxin poisoning.

The 53-year-old claimed on her podcast, The Jenny McCarthy Wahlberg Show , that she had fallen ill after spending time in an old dressing room with "air conditioning from 1950", believing that she was affected by the mold in the place.

Jenny added that she began to suffer a myriad of debilitating symptoms after her time in the dressing room, including a root canal infection, chalazions, rashes, swelling, insomnia, and small intestinal bacterial overgrowth.

She suspected that the air conditioning unit was the root of the problem after her makeup artist, "who only works on me in that dressing room", also started experiencing health issues.

After the ordeal, the TV personality felt the need to live in a tent outside her home, despite paying to have a specialist remove any mold in her house. "[I'm] paranoid now about basically sleeping anywhere," she shared, before showcasing her outdoor arrangements.

"I don't have to worry about rain in California, but I do worry about chemtrails and also sprinklers."

See Jenny with her husband, Donnie Wahlberg, below...

"You have to have the contractors come in and rebuild your house… and then you hear, you have to get rid of all your furniture, you have to get rid of all your clothes," Jenny continued.

"That's where this journey has brought me. After all those surgeries, after being diagnosed with mycotoxin poisoning, I feel a little bit sometimes crazy and like the walls are caving in and paranoid. It's really, really hard."

The mother of one felt that she even developed PTSD from the ordeal. "They talk about people with mold poisoning having PTSD. I'm still in the traumatic part. I'm not even in the 'post' part yet, because I feel like now everything is mold. I can detect mold, honestly, like a mold dog."

Jenny previously shared that she had to undergo nine separate surgeries on her mouth in 2025 due to a recurring infection that led to several of her teeth falling out.

Jenny and her husband, Donnie Wahlberg , listed their home in Chicago for $2.8 million in September and revealed their plans to move to Las Vegas.

The mansion features four bedrooms, six bathrooms, a sauna, a home gym, a theater, a waterslide and a hot tub, all spread over 1.3 acres.

"This isn't an extravagant home, but there's no greater symbol of our love for each other than this house and how much love has gone into it," Donnie told People of the abode.

"We made it a goal for ourselves and said it out loud because we wanted to make it happen. And here we are, together with our kids, and we're grateful for every bit of it."

articles.title: Sem os festivais criados e produzidos por Solano Ribeiro a partir de 1965, a MPB não teria surgido com tanta força | G1
articles.body:
Solano Ribeiro (1939 – 2026) foi nome fundamental na história da música brasileira por ter criado e/ou produzido importantes festivais — Foto: Divulgação

♬ Ocorrida na madrugada deste sábado, 31 de outubro de 2026, a morte do músico e produtor Solano Ribeiro, aos 87 anos, tira de cena um dos nomes mais importantes da história da música popular brasileira, em especial daquela música surgida nos anos 1960 e rotulada como MPB.

A atuação de Solano Ribeiro foi quase toda nos bastidores, mas foi tão decisiva que não é exagero dizer que, sem Solano, talvez a história da MPB fosse outra. Ou talvez nem existisse MPB da forma como ela foi caracterizada e organizada a partir de 1965, quase como se fosse um movimento.

É que Solano Ribeiro foi o idealizador e/ou produtor dos festivais mais relevantes realizados entre 1965 e 1972, período denominado como a era dos festivais. E os festivais foram a plataforma que deu projeção nacional a quase todos os gigantes da MPB por terem sido realizados e exibidos por emissoras de TV como Excelsior, Globo e Record.

Com exceção de Maria Bethânia, irrompida como furacão em fevereiro de 1965 no palco do show “Opinião”, todos os ícones daquela geração imbatível ganharam visibilidade e consolidaram as então iniciantes carreiras nos palcos dos festivais da canção – a começar por Elis Regina (1945 – 1982), cantora que venceu o I Festival de Música Popular Brasileira, produzido em 1965 pela TV Excelsior por iniciativa de Solano.

E é aí que entra a importância fundamental de Solano Ribeiro, menino paulistano nascido em 1939 que, na adolescência, se encantou pela música ao ganhar um violão de uma tia. Encanto que o levou ao rock'n'roll e, em 1957, ao posto de um dos vocalistas do grupo juvenil The Avallons, um dos primeiros conjuntos de rock da cidade de São Paulo (SP).

Mais tarde, nos anos 1960, quando já trabalhava na televisão, Solano ajudou a mudar o curso da história da música brasileira ao propor a criação dos festivais com inspiração no sucesso que o Festival de San Remo fazia na Itália com ecos em todo o universo pop ocidental.

Finda a era do rádio, a TV já começava a se tornar um veículo de massa e os festivais – produzidos entre as cidades de São Paulo (SP) e Rio de Janeiro (RJ), epicentros culturais do Brasil – contribuíram para a crescente hegemonia do veículo e para unir o país em torno da música.

Foram os festivais que, pela TV e com o apoio da indústria fonográfica, deram um rosto e uma voz a ídolos como Elis, Chico Buarque (revelação do festival de 1966), Caetano Veloso e Gilberto Gil (arquitetos da Tropicália, movimento deflagrado em antológico festival de 1967), Milton Nascimento (revelação no mesmo ano de 1967 na segunda edição do Festival Internacional da Canção, o FIC, assumido por Solano já na derradeira edição de 1972 que revelou Maria Alcina), Gal Costa (1945 – 2022) – divina, maravilhosa e roqueira em festival de 1968 – e Edu Lobo, entre outros grandes artistas, como Nana Caymmi (1941 – 2025), vaiada em 1966 ao defender a canção vencedora do primeiro FIC, “Saveiros” (Dori Caymmi e Nelson Motta, 1966).

Os festivais deram um sentido de movimento à música rotulada como MPB. Surgiu ali uma estética musical que se beneficiou da força dos festivais. Assim como os festivais também se alimentaram da força dessa geração excepcional que o tempo provou ser imbatível.

Solano Ribeiro, que se apaixonou por Elis Regina ainda em 1964, não descobriu essa geração, como fazia questão de ressaltar, mas abriu espaço para que ela florescesse.

“O papel de produtor para o qual eu me elegi foi mais o de um arquiteto e construtor de momentos emocionais, colocando artistas perante o público certo no momento certo”, resumiu Solano Ribeiro na introdução do livro de memórias do artista, “Prepare seu coração – Histórias da MPB”, editado em 2003.

Deu tão certo que não é exagero afirmar que a MPB não teria se projetado com tanta força e de forma tão instantânea na cena nacional sem os festivais cheios de som, fúria (dos perdedores) e paixão idealizados e/ou produzidos por Solano Ribeiro a partir de 1965.

articles.title: Shah Rukh Khan’s 'King' breaks overseas rights record at Rs 175 crore; eyes to top 'Pathaan', 'Jawan' collections to turn profitable
articles.summary: Even as big-budget South Indian films dominate the domestic market with their pan-India releases, Shah Rukh Khan continues to rule the overseas box office.
articles.body: Even as big-budget South Indian films dominate the domestic market with their pan-India releases, Shah Rukh Khan continues to rule the overseas box office. His upcoming film, 'King', is the latest proof. According to a new report, its overseas theatrical rights have been acquired for a staggering Rs 175 crore, setting a fresh record for Indian cinema. The deal highlights the actor’s unmatched global appeal and the enduring loyalty of his international fans.Phars Films pays record Rs 175 crore for Shah Rukh Khan’s ‘King’According to Pinkvilla, Phars Films has secured the overseas distribution rights for 'King' at Rs 175 crore, which is over $18 million. Until now, Yash Raj Films has handled the international release of Shah Rukh Khan’s films, successfully doing so for both 'Pathaan', produced under its own banner, and 'Jawan' in 2023. Phars, however, is no newcomer to the overseas market. It has worked alongside YRF on several titles and independently distributed Prabhas’ 'Saaho'. The report adds that Phars has paid a minimum guarantee of Rs 175 crore for the rights. Considering that no Indian film has crossed the Rs 100 crore mark overseas so far, the figure is truly staggering.What Shah Rukh Khan’s ‘King’ must earn to break evenThe minimum guarantee a distributor pays reflects the distributor's confidence in a film’s box-office run. Since overseas distributors typically keep just 50% of the gross, King would need to collect roughly $37-40 million, or about Rs 350-375 crore, internationally merely to break even. For perspective, Khan’s biggest hits, 'Pathaan' and 'Jawan', each brought in close to Rs 400 crore abroad, so 'King' must match that, or better it, to turn a profit. With such a steep guarantee, the film’s overseas earnings would need to rival those of 'Dhurandhar 2' (₹460 crore) or 'RRR' (Rs 430 crore), both among the biggest international successes Indian cinema has ever seen.Shah Rukh Khan’s ‘King’: Cast, director and release dateDirected by Siddharth Anand, 'King' has Shah Rukh Khan headlining the cast, reuniting the pair after their 2023 hit Pathaan. The ensemble also includes Deepika Padukone, Abhishek Bachchan, Rani Mukerji, Jaideep Ahlawat, Raghav Juyal and Saurabh Shukla. Notably, the film brings Shah Rukh together on screen with his daughter Suhana Khan for the first time, following her acting debut in The Archies in 2023. articles.title: Zaheer Iqbal says he and Sonakshi Sinha got several romantic film offers but picked 'Tu Hai Meri Kiran' for its shock value instead of repeating what 'we do on Instagram'
articles.summary: Zaheer Iqbal and his wife Sonakshi Sinha are loved for their playful chemistry and sweet social media moments.
articles.body: Zaheer Iqbal and his wife Sonakshi Sinha are loved for their playful chemistry and sweet social media moments. But the couple surprised fans by coming together for the thriller ‘Tu Hai Meri Kiran’, in which Zaheer plays a possessive lover. In a recent interview, the actor spoke about the film, his bond with Sonakshi and his Bollywood debut, which was backed by Salman Khan.Zaheer Iqbal on his role in ‘Tu Hai Meri Kiran’In a chat with Midday, Zaheer Iqbal said a lot of effort went into building his character. He shared, “We shot a lot. We shot extra stuff, and, on the edit, we had to remove certain things to simplify it or to make it less obvious sometimes. I did a lot of workshops, and I worked really hard on this character because it’s one opportunity that you get sometimes to do a character like this, and you don’t want to mess it up.”Choosing a different on-screen dynamicThe couple consciously chose not to play the cute and sweet pair that audiences know from their real life. Zaheer said, “If we did what we do off-screen or we do on Instagram, you’ll feel like you’re in a theatre scrolling on reels and you’ll want to be like swipe up.” He added that they had got many offers to play a romantic couple, but this film stood out for its shock value.In the film, their characters move from being engaged to being married. Zaheer explained, “So half the film, we were engaged and married for the other half.” He also praised Sonakshi, saying, “She is just so seasoned in what she does.”Is Zaheer Iqbal a possessive partner?On possessiveness in relationships, Zaheer feels it depends on the equation between two people and how secure they make each other feel. He said, “A lot of people are just inherently obsessive and possessive. But I think in a normal relationship like me and Sona, I feel it’s your partner who can make you possessive or not.”On the idea of equality, he said Sonakshi is superior. He explained, “I don’t believe men and women are equal. I believe women are way more superior because one can never be stronger than a woman who gave you birth.”On facing trollsZaheer Iqbal said the couple does not give much weight to online trolling. “I don’t see anything bad. I don’t feel we get trolled that much. And if we feel, we don’t pay attention,” he said.How Salman Khan gave him his first breakZaheer also recalled how he got into films after Salman Khan saw him dancing at his sister’s wedding. The offer came without warning, and he remains thankful for it. He said, “I was dancing somewhere at a wedding. My sister’s wedding, and Salman Khan happened to be there and offer me a film. So, it worked out that way. I got my chance. And it literally fell in my lap. And I don’t take that for granted ever. I don’t think there’s anybody else like that. In the industry right now, if you think there must be two or three people who were spotted like this. I’m glad I’m blessed.”Directed by Karan Rawal, 'Tu Hai Meri Kiran' was released in theatres on October 23, 2026.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Kajol, Sanjay Dutt, Raveena Tandon and others mourn filmmaker Sanjay Gupta's demise: 'Gone too soon'
articles.summary: Actors, including Kajol, Raveena Tandon and Sanjay Dutt, remembered \"full-of-life filmmaker\" Sanjay Gupta, whose credits include films such as \"Kaante\",
articles.body: Actors, including Kajol, Raveena Tandon and Sanjay Dutt, remembered "full-of-life filmmaker" Sanjay Gupta, whose credits include films such as "Kaante", "Shootout at Lokhandwala" and "Mumbai Saga", among others.Gupta died at his residence after he slipped and hit his head.Kajol shared a picture of the filmmaker on her Instagram handle on Saturday and said the news of Gupta's demise was "heartbreaking". "Sending love and immense strength to the family through this loss. Rest in peace," she wrote.Sanjay Dutt shared a series of pictures alongside the filmmaker with whom he has collaborated on films such as "Aatish: Feel the Fire" and "Kaante", among others."Gupts, my brother. I still cannot believe that you are gone. We have shared so much together, so many memories and so many years of friendship. You have always been family to me, and that will never change," he wrote.Dutt recalled his discussion about "Kante 2" with the filmmaker and said he will make the film in his memory."I will miss you, our conversations and all the times we spent together. We were just discussing 'Kante 2' recently, I will make 'Kaante 2' your dream, in memory of you my brother, I will do everything for this dream of yours to come true, love you forever and always. Life will not be the same without you, brother," he added.Tandon said, "Shocked to hear the shocking news of the untimely passing od dar Gups. Really saddened #sanjaygupta."Anupam Kher said Gupta was a "filmmaker with a distinctive style and an enormous love for cinema"."Woke up in Stockholm to the heartbreaking news of my friend and director Sanjay Gupta. You could ask him practically anything about movies, and a conversation with him would remind you how much he loved the world he belonged to. His passion came through in his social media posts too, where, of late, he had been expressing himself so openly. I worked with him in two films. But he also holds a special place in our family's journey. He was Sikandar's first director," he wrote.Kher said he was an "encyclopedia of films". "Kher saab, we must work together!"That was almost always his opening line whenever we met. He said it when I last met him, about a year ago. We always think there will be time. Another meeting. Another conversation. Another film. It hurts to know that this one will remain unfinished.I remember his warmth, his affection, and a lovely Holi party at his home few years back," he added.Hansal Mehta shared a picture alongside Gupta on his Instagram handle along with a note and said they went through many lows and highs together. "Not done, bro. Sanjay Gupta. Gups. My only boss in the film industry, perhaps. But more than that, a dear friend. We went through many lows and many highs together, and through all of it we shared a love for the good things in life," he wrote."My first and only Rolex came from him. Today it's the one memory of him I carry on my wrist, and I don't think I'll ever take it off. He held my hand when I was at my lowest. We didn't exactly create magic together, but the time itself was an absolute blast..."I watched some of the best films of my life in his theatre. I borrowed some of the best books I've read from his shelves. My bro code began with you, Sanjay. And now it is ended," he added.Kunal Kohli said, "Don't know how to process this news. #SanjayGupta RIP. Chatted with him little over a month ago. We were both on an awards show jury couple of years ago - we were equally quick to have an argument & a laugh about it later. You had many more films and many years to go. Prayers and strength to the family," in the post.Dia Mirza, who has worked with Gupta on "Dus Kahaniyaan", shared a picture of the filmmaker on her Instagram story and said she is grateful for their collaboration."Sanjay Gupta, I will always be grateful for the work we did together, the love, the respect and the support I got from you. RIP Gupta Saab. Deepest condolences to the family," she wrote.Neil Nitin Mukesh said he is "deeply saddened and shocked" by the death of Gupta. "A powerhouse filmmaker we all loved and respected. Gone far too soon. My heartfelt condolences to his family and loved ones."Tusshar Kapoor uploaded a note on his X handle and said "Woke up to sad news about the unfortunate and sudden demise of my beloved director @_SanjayGupta," he wrote."Life is so unpredictable, though this man was a lesson learned in living life to the fullest! My deepest condolences to his family, RIP sir," he added."Deeply saddened by this tragic news. May his soul rest in eternal peace," Madhur Bhandarkar said.Kangana Ranaut shared a picture of the actor on her Instagram story as she remembered him. "Sanjay Gupta jis demise has sent shock waves across the film industry, extremely sad and horrific news, have worked with him closely and what is unsettling is that he was not even unwell, terrible," she said.Lyricist and poet Manoj Muntashir recalled his collaboration with the director. "We only worked together in two films, one of which was-'Kaabil'. In the time we spent together, I learned that Sanjay was not just an outstanding filmmaker, but also an incredible friend," he wrote.Navjot Gulati said Gupta was among the most "funny and full-of-life filmmakers". "It is unbelievable that @_SanjayGupta is no more with us," he wrote."Other than being a filmmaker who made many COOL movies, his insights on life and the business of movies were a thing of beauty. And a true blue cinephile. RIP Sir. Oopar Kisi Screening room mein milege," he added.Gupta is known for making action-thriller and crime films such as "Aatish", "Kaabil", "Shootout at Lokhandwala", "Shootout at Wadala", "Jazbaa", "Zinda", and "Mumbai Saga", among others.He is survived by his wife, Anuradha Lekhi Gupta, and their children, Shivaansh Gupta and Dalai Gupta.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Sanjay Gupta passes away: Fardeen Khan, Ronit Roy, Rakesh Roshan and others pay last respects at filmmaker's Mumbai residence
articles.summary: Following the news of filmmaker Sanjay Gupta's demise on Saturday morning, several friends and members of the film fraternity gathered at his Mumbai
articles.body: Following the news of filmmaker Sanjay Gupta's demise on Saturday morning, several friends and members of the film fraternity gathered at his Mumbai residence to pay their last respects.Among those spotted arriving at the filmmaker's residence were actors Fardeen Khan, Ronit Roy, Rohit Roy and Gulshan Grover, filmmaker Rakesh Roshan, director Milap Zaveri, actor Sudhanshu Pandey and filmmaker Ashoke Pandit, among others.Ronit Roy and Milap Zaveri appeared visibly emotional, with tears in their eyes as they mourned the filmmaker’s demise.Sanjay Gupta, best known for directing films such as 'Kaante' and 'Shootout at Lokhandwala', passed away at the age of 57.As per Mumbai Police, Producer Sanjay Gupta, residing within the jurisdiction of the Versova Police Station, passed away late last night. He reportedly lost his balance and fell inside his home, sustaining a head injury that led to bleeding and, ultimately, his death. He lived in the bungalow with his wife, two children, and a domestic help; however, as everyone was asleep at the time, the incident was only discovered this morning. The family has expressed no suspicions or complaints. The body has been sent for a post-mortem examination.According to Mumbai Police, Sanjay Gupta, who resided within the jurisdiction of Versova Police Station, passed away late on Friday night after reportedly losing his balance and falling inside his residence. He sustained a head injury that resulted in bleeding and ultimately led to his death.As per the police, Gupta was living in the bungalow with his wife, two children and a domestic help. However, since everyone was asleep at the time of the incident, it was discovered only on Saturday morning.The family has reportedly expressed no suspicion or raised any complaint regarding the circumstances surrounding his death. His body has been sent for a post-mortem examination.Further details regarding his funeral are awaited.On the professional front, his last directorial venture was The Miranda Brothers, starring Harshvardhan Rane and Meezaan Jafri, which was released in 2024. As a producer, he also came up with 'Visfot', featuring Fardeen Khan and Riteish Deshmukh. Before that, he directed Mumbai Saga (2021), starring John Abraham and Emraan Hashmi in lead roles.However, Gupta was widely recognised for directing crime dramas such as 'Shootout at Lokhandwala' and 'Kaante', which established his presence in the crime thriller genre.His other directorial ventures included 'Kaabil' and 'Shootout at Wadala'.Known for his work in action and crime-based films, Gupta made a significant contribution to Hindi cinema through his distinctive storytelling and films centred on crime, action and drama.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Young artists turn to handmade forms to explore memory, identity and ecology
articles.summary: Ten emerging artists working with materials ranging from clay and glass to textiles, natural dyes, wood and reclaimed rubber are part of Insubordinate
articles.body: Ten emerging artists working with materials ranging from clay and glass to textiles, natural dyes, wood and reclaimed rubber are part of Insubordinate Matter, the sixth edition of Emami Art’s annual IMAGINARIUM open-call exhibition. On display at Gallery 2 and 3 of Emami Art until December 26, the exhibition brings together practices that explore the relationship between material, memory, the body and the natural environment.Launched in 2020, IMAGINARIUM was conceived to support young and emerging visual artists through awards, exhibitions and mentorship. This year, the open call received more than 1,200 portfolios, which were reviewed by a jury comprising artist Ibrahim Mahama, May Makki, Siddharth Somaiya, Shaunak Mahbubani and Emami Art director and head curator Ushmita Sahu. Ten artists were selected for the exhibition, with three receiving the annual awards.Bhagyashri Dange received the first award of Rs 2 lakh, followed by Sonu Pujar, who received the second award of Rs 1.5 lakh, and Subhash Deka, who received the third award of Rs 1 lakh. The awards are supported by the Emami Foundation and Kolkata Centre for Creativity.The exhibition takes the position that material is not merely a medium for artistic expression but can also hold memory and carry meaning. The works examine two broad concerns: the body and its inherited histories, and the natural world under pressure. Through handmade and often tactile forms, the artists explore questions of identity, gender, ecology, labour and collective memory.“The strength of this year’s cohort lies in its materiality. These are artists who think through substance, through clay and glass, cloth, wood and reclaimed matter, and who treat the made object not as a surface for ideas but as something living, that holds memory and carries a fragile world,” said Sahu.The participating artists approach these concerns through varied practices. Dange works across drawing, painting and printmaking to examine the body as a site of memory and conditioning, while Pujar uses textiles, organic matter and domestic materials to explore gendered labour, care and personal histories. Deka draws on natural rhythms and environmental phenomena to create sculptural works reflecting the relationship between people and their surroundings.Other artists bring distinct material approaches to the exhibition. Srijita Raha works with textiles and natural dyes to explore girlhood, vulnerability and psychological space. Annanya Dhanda draws on domestic objects and familial histories, particularly mother-daughter relationships, while Ayushi Shukla engages with traditional visual languages and the cultural memory of the Ganga.The remaining participants are Tithi Das, whose paintings draw on archival photographs and emotional inheritance; Dibbya Mudi, who transforms discarded industrial rubber through weaving and stitching; Shibayan Halder, whose multidisciplinary practice examines environmental change and the relationship between people and place; and Siya Raju, who works with ceramics and glass to explore natural forms and human relationships.Speaking about the initiative, Richa Agarwal, founder-director of Emami Art, said the open call was established to address the gap between artistic talent and the opportunities available to young practitioners. “What matters to us is not recognition alone, but giving emerging artists the standing and the support a young practice needs at the moment it is most fragile,” she said.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: Director Sasi's romantic drama 'Nooru Kodi Vaanavil', starring Harish Kalyan and Siddhi Idnani, is finally set to reach audiences after a long wait for
articles.body: Director Sasi's romantic drama 'Nooru Kodi Vaanavil', starring Harish Kalyan and Siddhi Idnani, is finally set to reach audiences after a long wait for its theatrical release. The film will now premiere directly on OTT. The film, which explores love, family relationships, and difficult life choices, is now set to premiere directly on OTT. The makers have announced that the film will stream on ZEE5 from November 6 as a special Diwali release.Sasi clarifies why 'Nooru Kodi Vaanavil' did not release in theatresDuring a recent interaction with Behindwoods, both Sasi and Harish Kalyan were asked why the film was not released in theatres despite its promising trailer. Responding to the question, director Sasi clarified that the decision had nothing to do with the creative aspects of the film. He said, "For some reasons, which we could not say or avoid, there was no creative side to it. From the production side, they felt that bringing the film directly to OTT would give us better results. His statement made it clear that the decision was taken entirely by the production team.Harish Kalyan says it was painful to wait for the film's releaseHarish Kalyan also shared his feelings about the film finally reaching viewers, although it missed a theatrical release. Comparing a film to a child, the actor explained how difficult it was to wait for it to reach audiences. He said, "A film is like a child. There is a pain when it does not reach anyone. articles.title: Studios destroyed, traditions saved: Artists fight to save Sudan’s culture
articles.summary: Artists in Sudan are working to save culture and traditions amid the country’s war.
articles.body:
Port Sudan, Sudan – Awad Haroun, 45, a visual artist and theatre director, fled his home in Al-Halfaya, Khartoum North, after war destroyed a life he had worked hard to build in the capital.

He moved to Port Sudan with his wife and son, leaving behind his home, artistic workspace and the tools he needed to work, shortly after fighting erupted between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and Rapid Support Forces (RSF) paramilitary in April 2023.

When he fled, he carried little: Two shirts, two pairs of trousers, two books and a few torn drawing papers, expecting to return soon. Instead, he has been forced to rebuild his life far from home.

He lost not only his home but also the tools and materials he relied on to work and make a living.

In Port Sudan, he looked to use his skills in sculpture, design and decoration for some money. He has since participated in theatrical performances at Wasel Festival, organised by Ahalina Cultural Group in partnership with UNESCO, and led traditional arts workshops with cultural groups.

Awad founded Ahalina cultural group in 2013 with a group of young people, using theatre, visual arts, music and puppetry to engage with young people and promote peace and social cohesion.

Drawing, storytelling, music and play have also given children opportunities to express themselves and connect with others.

“Losing my tools does not mean I have lost my skills, and losing my workspace does not mean I have lost my ability to create,” Awad told Al Jazeera.

Awad and other displaced artists found shelter at an old school in Port Sudan, where they helped clean and prepare the building for families forced from their homes.

“Now, concerns about the possibility of eviction have left us uncertain about where we will go next,” he said.

While art cannot replace a lost home or end the war, Awad believes it can preserve memories, bring communities together and offer children space to play and express themselves.

“From the ashes, we will rise” is the motto of Ahalina cultural group. This is more than a slogan for Awad; it is a reminder to keep creating, despite everything the war has taken from him.

The war has taken a heavy toll on Sudan’s cultural life, damaging heritage sites and disrupting the livelihoods of artists across the country.

In June 2026, UNESCO estimated that Sudan’s cultural sector faced a $30m funding gap. But behind this figure are deeply personal losses: Artists killed by the war or forced to leave behind studios, galleries, artworks and the tools they need to create.

In April 2024, UNESCO reported that the Artists and Writers Union in Port Sudan had provided shelter to more than 112 displaced artists and other cultural professionals.

The challenges remain significant, but cultural initiatives have continued. In April 2026, UNESCO said its initiatives in Port Sudan had benefitted more than 350 artists, women, girls and internally displaced cultural professionals, supporting efforts to sustain Sudan’s cultural life amid the conflict.

Asim Abdelaziz, 31, a musician and filmmaker, left El Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan state, amid escalating fighting and repeated drone attacks. He arrived in Port Sudan in November 2023, hoping to find safety and work.

Separated from his family, who are scattered between Omdurman and El Obeid, Asim lives alone in a shelter for displaced artists. The war has uprooted his life and disrupted his career, but he continues to use music to preserve Sudan’s cultural heritage and bring communities together.

In Port Sudan, he has worked with the local Artists and Writers Union, UNESCO and community organisations. He has also collaborated with the Ministry of Culture and Information and other artists on music programmes to address social issues, including hate speech and racism.

Asim said the war has spurred hate speech and deepened divisions between Sudan’s different communities. He believes art can counter these differences by promoting diversity, mutual acceptance and peaceful coexistence.

“I have seen firsthand how hate speech affects people’s lives,” Asim told Al Jazeera. “Through music, I try to remind Sudanese people that we are all brothers and sisters, and that war does not represent who we are.”

Mokhalaya, a project he founded to document and archive traditional music and rhythms from across the country a year ago, is one avenue for this.

“I hope to take the project to international festivals, introducing audiences abroad to [showcase] Sudan’s rich musical traditions and cultural diversity,” he said.

Preserving heritage is not just about safeguarding the past, but also about keeping Sudan’s cultural identity alive during a war that has displaced communities and disrupted lives, he said.

Abdelqader Hashem, secretary of the Red Sea State Writers and Artists Union, told Al Jazeera the union has supported artists and their families who fled fighting in other parts of Sudan since the war began on April 15, 2023.

“We worked to establish a shelter for displaced artists in a school in Port Sudan and sought support from local and international organisations to provide for their basic needs,” he said.

Beyond providing shelter, the union has helped displaced artists take part in the city’s cultural activities, contributing to community awareness programmes that address important societal issues such as the dangers of drug use, a growing concern in Sudan.

“We have also implemented projects in partnership with UNESCO to train children in displacement camps in handicrafts, including concrete crafts,” Hashem said.

“Most of the displaced artists have since returned to their homes in Khartoum following the Sudanese army’s recapture of the capital.”

articles.title: Ajay Devgn moves to Bombay High Court, challenges FDA's notice which was sent to him, Shah Rukh Khan, Tiger Shroff over Elaichi ad, plea to be heard on November 4
articles.summary: Actor Ajay Devgn has approached the Bombay High Court challenging the show-cause notice issued to him by the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration
articles.body: Actor Ajay Devgn has approached the Bombay High Court challenging the show-cause notice issued to him by the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) over his endorsement of Vimal Elaichi in a television advertisement.According to PTI, Devgn has argued in his petition that the notice was wrongly directed at him in his capacity as an actor instead of being issued to the manufacturing company. A division bench comprising Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna is expected to hear the matter on November 4.In his petition, Ajay Devgn has strongly challenged the FDA's show-cause notice, alleging that the authority had already made up its mind before seeking his explanation. The plea states that although the communication was issued as a show-cause notice, it effectively amounted to a decision already taken by the FDA."Though styled a 'Show Cause Notice', the Impugned SCN is, in substance, a decision or order already taken by the FDA that the issuance of such a notice is a gross abuse of the process of law. A bare perusal of the Impugned SCN makes it abundantly evident that the same has been issued with a premeditated and predetermined mind, and calling upon the Petitioner to show cause against it is a mere farce and an empty formality, since the issuing authority has already reached its conclusion, which is evident from the directions passed against the Petitioner. The Impugned SCN is also ex facie violative of Article 14 of the Constitution of India and of the principles of natural justice. The Impugned SCN is mala fide, patently illegal and wholly arbitrary and would inter alia cause grave and irreparable harm to the Petitioner's reputation and profession," the plea reads.Devgn had also submitted a response to the show-cause notice in September, maintaining that he had appeared only in an advertisement promoting Vimal Elaichi and had not endorsed Vimal Pan Masala.The Maharashtra FDA had earlier issued notices to Ajay Devgn, Shah Rukh Khan and Tiger Shroff for featuring in advertisements for Vimal Elaichi, alleging that the campaigns indirectly promoted Vimal Pan Masala, a chewable product prohibited in the state.Explaining the grounds for its action, the FDA stated in its notice: “Upon examination of the said advertisement, it prima facie appears that the advertisement promotes the Vimal brand, which is mainly associated with Pan Masala, a product prohibited for manufacture, storage, transportation, distribution, and sale in the State of Maharashtra for a period of one year, with effect from the date specified in the Prohibition Order dated the 13th July, 2026, issued by the Commissioner of Food Safety, Maharashtra State, under Section 30(2)(a) of the FSS Act, 2006."The notices were delivered at different addresses. Devgn was served at his Juhu residence, while Shah Rukh Khan received his notice at Mannat in Bandra. In Tiger Shroff's case, the notice was sent through his production company, Tiger Shroff Productions LLP.The notices triggered considerable controversy, although none of the three actors has publicly commented on the matter so far.The FDA has invoked Section 24 of the Food Safety and Standards (FSS) Act, 2006, which prohibits misleading or deceptive advertisements concerning food products. The action also forms part of the regulator's broader drive to address food safety violations across Maharashtra.As part of this exercise, the FDA has been conducting checks against food and milk adulteration, monitoring the sale of unhealthy food near schools and cracking down on banned gutka and tobacco-based pan masala. The department has also intensified inspections and seizures in recent months, taking action against establishments and individuals found violating food safety regulations.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Michael Douglas Gives Update on Jack Nicholson: He’s ‘Well’ But Has ‘Disappeared’
articles.summary: "He is up there by his house and walking around in his slippers," actor says of his longtime friend. "He deserves it."
articles.body:
Michael Douglas has provided an update on his friend Jack Nicholson, saying the legendary actor — who hasn't appeared on the big screen in 16 years — is "well" but has "disappeared."

Douglas and Nicholson's friendship began in the mid-1970s, when Douglas served as producer on One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest , starring Nicholson in an Oscar-winning role.

Speaking in Swansea, Wales while promoting his memoir One Helluva Ride , Douglas said that he wished he and Nicholson shared the screen together. I would have liked to have acted with Jack," Douglas said ( via People ). "He's not working any more. He's well. He has disappeared. I know that."

Nicholson last appeared on the big screen in 2010's How Do You Know .

"I still see him, but he is fine," Douglas added. "He is up there by his house and walking around in his slippers. It happens. He deserves it. I understand. He is a few years older than me, but I understand."

Nicholson has dramatically cut back on public appearances in recent years, only attending the rare Los Angeles Lakers game now and then . However, the actor made a surprise onscreen appearance in 2025 to introduce Adam Sandler on Saturday Night Live 's 50th anniversary episode; Nicholson previously served in a similar capacity during the SNL 40 show in 2015.

articles.body: Filmmaker Sanjay Gupta known for movies like 'Kaante', 'Aatish', 'Shootout At Wadala', 'Shootout At Lokhandwala' among others passed away on October 30 after sustaining a head injury at his Mumbai residence. Filmmaker Ashoke Pandit confirmed the news on X, expressing shock over the sudden loss of his friend.'It's really shocking and sad. Just got the news that our dear friend an ace director @_sanjaygupta is no more. He passed due to a head injury at home. Another talent gone too soon. Sanjay had excitedly shared that the original film with the same title was produced by his father. Milap announced that he would dedicate the project to him, writing, "That title. This film. articles.title: Former Miss USA contestant made a life-changing decision at 26 after cancer devastated family
articles.summary: Allyn Rose lost nearly every woman in her family to breast cancer before choosing a preventive double mastectomy that even sparked hate mail.
articles.body: At age 26, Allyn Rose made a life-changing decision after cancer had devastated her family. The model, who competed in both the Miss America and Miss USA pageants, underwent a preventive double mastectomy, a decision she said even sparked "hate mail" from critics. Today, the mother of two is the founder of The Previvor, a nonprofit organization that educates women about breast cancer risk and prevention options. Oct. 31 marks the last day of Breast Cancer Awareness Month. "I know a lot of people think that's a pretty radical choice for someone who hadn't been diagnosed with breast cancer yet," Rose, now 38, told Fox News Digital. "But I lost my mom when I was 16. And by the time I was 16, I had lost my grandmother, my great aunt, almost every woman in my family to this disease. And I said that legacy ends with me." KAI TRUMP REVEALS HOW FAMILY RALLIED AROUND MOM VANESSA AMID BREAST CANCER BATTLE: ‘IT’S A LONG JOURNEY’ "I don't want that to be my story," she said. "I don't want to have to tell my 16-year-old daughter someday that she's going to have to spend the rest of her life without her mom. This sad family legacy was not going to take my life if I had anything to do with it." Rose's mother, Judy Rose, was first diagnosed with breast cancer at 27 and had her right breast removed. The cancer later developed in her remaining breast, reaching stage 3, according to People magazine. Judy died at 51. Breast cancer is the most common cancer among women in the U.S. after skin cancers, accounting for about 1 in 3 new cancer cases diagnosed in women each year, according to the American Cancer Society. About 1 in 8 U.S. women will develop breast cancer during their lives. WATCH: ALLYN ROSE CHOSE DOUBLE MASTECTOMY AT 26 SO CANCER LEGACY 'ENDS WITH ME' The organization estimates that 321,910 new cases of invasive breast cancer will be diagnosed among U.S. women in 2026 and that about 42,140 women will die from the disease. FOX NEWS MEDIA TEAMS UP WITH BREAST CANCER RESEARCH FOUNDATION Rose was considered at elevated risk of developing breast cancer because of her extensive family history. In 2012, she was crowned Miss District of Columbia, earning the opportunity to represent the district at the 2013 Miss America pageant. That same year, at 24, Rose announced her decision to undergo a preventive double mastectomy. She had the surgery two years later, at 26. For women with a strong family history of breast cancer, a bilateral risk-reducing mastectomy can lower the risk of developing the disease by up to 90%, according to the National Cancer Institute. The procedure does not eliminate the risk entirely because it is impossible to remove all breast tissue that could become cancerous. "So much of my life and my identity was wrapped up in the way that I looked and how I presented myself to the world," Rose said. "I paid my bills and my rent with the way that I looked. It would very likely end my modeling career, my career in pageantry, my career really in the entertainment industry. articles.title: Richard Simmons’ Hollywood Hills home finally sells for $3.8 million  , lot less than the asking price
articles.summary: Richard Simmons' iconic Hollywood Hills home sold for $3.8 million after several price reductions. The property, rich in history and character, features unique architecture and was significant in Simmons' private life. Find out more about the sale and Simmons' legacy.
articles.body: Richard Simmons’ longtime Los Angeles home has a new owner. It sold for $3,827,500, more than two years after the fitness star died in July 2024. He lived there for most of his adult life, so this sale really does close a chapter on a house that was a big part of who he was.It first went on the market in June 2025 at nearly $7 million. After a few price cuts, it came off the market for a bit, then came back in April 2026 at about $5.8 million. It still sold for way less than where it started.According to PEOPLE, the buyer fell for the home’s history and wants to bring back its classic character. Listing agent Rachelle Rosten talked about the sale and the buyer’s plans with Realtor.com.Simmons bought the place in the 1980s and stayed for roughly forty years. It’s perched above the Sunset Strip, was built in 1937 and is a NeoClassical Revival Colonial. You get four bedrooms and four and a half bathrooms across 4,977 square feet, plus city views and lots of privacy.From the outside, it’s formal and traditional. Step inside, though, and you get a real sense of who lived there. This is where Simmons spent most of his private life, especially after he stepped away from the spotlight in 2014. After years of cameras, studio audiences and crowds of people trying to get fit, the house became his refuge.A cherub staircase and a pool shaped like a keyThis is not your average Hollywood Hills mansion. The staircase is lined with cherub sculptures, and there’s patterned wallpaper, curved French patio doors and traditional living and dining rooms.There’s also a big primary suite, a guest suite with its own entrance, an office and a gym in the attic. Fitting, really, for a man who made his living getting people off the couch. Terraced gardens, an open lawn and a key-shaped swimming pool complete the grounds, which definitely don’t feel like a cookie-cutter luxury estate.Rosten pointed to these quirks when she explained why the house appealed. She told to Realtor.com that the buyer was drawn to its “rich history, heritage, and pedigree” and plans to restore it to its classic roots.From almost $7 million to $3.8 millionThe sale took a while. The house hit the market in June 2025, almost a year after Simmons passed away. The asking price got cut several times, and in February 2026 it was pulled from the market altogether. It returned in April at around $5.799 million, and the final price of $3,827,500 ended up well below where it began.The buyer seems to want more than just a good address in a sought-after area. Planning to restore the house suggests they want to keep its character.The house belongs to someone else now, but Simmons’ story will always be part of the house’s story. The place where he spent so much of his private life gets a chance to start fresh.Who was Richard Simmons?Richard Simmons was born Milton Teagle Simmons on July 12, 1948, in New Orleans, Louisiana. He was an American fitness personality, TV personality and author, known for his energy, flamboyant costumes and friendly approach to exercise. His Sweatin’ to the Oldies workout videos got lots of people moving as part of their everyday lives. In 1974, he opened a Beverly Hills fitness studio, Slimmons. He passed away at his Los Angeles home on July 13, 2024, a day after his 76th birthday.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Tim McGraw says brutal toll of filming 'Yellowstone' prequel pushed him to edge: 'Wouldn't have survived'
articles.summary: Between 14-hour days and late-night flights for concerts, Tim McGraw says filming Taylor Sheridan's "1883" was the hardest job he and Faith Hill ever had.
articles.body: Tim McGraw was pushed to the brink while filming Taylor Sheridan's Western drama "1883." The country music superstar revealed that the brutal production schedule left him questioning how much longer he could keep going. Between 14-hour shooting days, six-day workweeks and late-night flights for concert performances, McGraw said the grueling experience was unlike anything he and his wife, Faith Hill, had faced before. "If it had gone on any longer, I probably wouldn't have survived, put it that way," McGraw told Esquire. MATTHEW MCCONAUGHEY GIVES UPDATE ON RUMORED 'YELLOWSTONE' SPIN-OFF SERIES, YEARS AFTER REPORTS FIRST SURFACED The "Live Like You Were Dying" singer described the demands of filming the "Yellowstone" prequel. "I learned a lot, certainly because it was such a tough shoot," McGraw said. "I think we shot for right around six months. It was a long shoot. Five or six months. It was close to it. And we shot mostly six days a week, and like 14 hours a day." But filming wasn't McGraw's only commitment. The country star was also juggling concerts, sometimes going straight from the set to an airplane before returning home in the middle of the night and starting the cycle again just hours later. "And during that time, I had a handful of shows that I had to do," he explained. "So there were times that I would finish up around six o'clock in the evening, jump on a plane, go do a show and then get home at 1:00 in the morning, then be in the gym at 3:00 and be in the makeup chair at 5:30, 6:00. So, I had a few of those." Although "1883" followed the Duttons' journey from Texas to Montana, much of the series was filmed in Texas before production moved north. The cast also endured a rigorous cowboy camp, learning to ride, rope, work cattle and shoot guns before filming began. "We all got to do it together, which was an incredible experience," "1883" co-star Eric Nelsen previously told Fox News Digital. "But it was a time for us to get comfortable on our horses, to learn how to cut cattle, how to rope, how to shoot guns – all the things we're going to have to do on the show." The real test came on set. McGraw and Hill recalled filming a dangerous river crossing around 3 a.m. on their 25th wedding anniversary, with temperatures hovering around 36 or 37 degrees, according to Entertainment Weekly. The grueling schedule left little room for sleep or recovery. "I told Faith it was probably the hardest job we've ever had. I had some hard jobs growing up." McGraw then revealed how close the demanding schedule had pushed him to his limit. Despite the physical demands, McGraw said the experience was worth it, particularly because he got to work alongside Hill and Sheridan. MICHELLE PFEIFFER FOUGHT 'BATTLE' WITH TAYLOR SHERIDAN BEFORE SURRENDERING TO HIT SHOW 'THE MADISON' "It was tough, but it was worth it because we were getting to work together, and we were getting to work with Taylor, who was fantastic, and like I said, a brilliant writer." McGraw also said he gained a greater appreciation for preparation, explaining that the demanding production taught him the importance of arriving on set ready to work. Although McGraw had previously appeared in films, "1883" marked his first major role in a television series.The demanding shoot also required McGraw to contend with unpredictable conditions on set. "But I think I learned more than anything is there's so much value in preparing. articles.title: Pony Verma on marrying Prakash Raj despite 12-year age gap, bonding with his daughters from first marriage: 'There is calmness that he brought into my life'
articles.summary: Choreographer Pony Verma has opened up about her marriage to actor Prakash Raj, sharing how their 12-year age difference, which initially raised concerns
articles.body: Choreographer Pony Verma has opened up about her marriage to actor Prakash Raj, sharing how their 12-year age difference, which initially raised concerns among some of her friends, turned out to be an important aspect of their relationship. She believes the actor's life experiences helped him understand her better and brought a sense of stability into her life.Pony recalled how some of her friends were unhappy with her decision to marry a man who was 12 years older than her. However, she never saw the age gap as a disadvantage. “My friends were mad because I was marrying a man who was 12 years older than me," she said.Explaining why she was comfortable with the difference in their ages, Pony said Prakash's experiences allowed him to understand her journey, struggles and perspective on life. “But I feel happy that we have a 12-year gap because I think a man like Prakash could really understand me and the depth of my life, where I have come from, how I think, and how I struggled," she said.She also spoke about the sense of reassurance and emotional stability that Prakash brought into her life, saying his presence helped her look at things more calmly. “There is calmness that Prakash Raj brought into my life. So just sit back, enjoy the food, it’s all good. Nothing is going away, no time is running out, you’re not falling behind in life. Everything will work out," Pony said.She further added, “Honestly, only a guy who’s been through what Prakash Raj has could’ve handled me well." Pony also recalled what attracted her to Prakash when they first started getting to know each other. According to her, the actor never made an effort to impress her through extravagant gestures or by pretending to be someone he was not.“He was very honest with his approach," she said. “He never tried to impress me. He never tried to make it all flashy for me, a girl from Mumbai. No, he was just himself, really simple. That’s what I loved about him."She revealed that Prakash was equally straightforward about his expectations from their relationship and had made his intentions clear from the outset. “One thing was very clear from Prakash Raj. He said he wants a long-term relationship. ‘I want to get married, and that’s just how it is. I’m not here to waste time,’" she recalled.Pony also spoke about the bond she shares with Prakash's daughters, Pooja and Meghana, from his first marriage. She described their relationship as affectionate and said they have remained an integral part of the family over the years. “Pooja and Meghana keep coming home," she said. Recalling their presence at her wedding, Pony said both daughters actively participated in the ceremonies and stood by the couple during the celebrations.“On the wedding day, they were standing in front of me during the ceremony, putting mehendi and haldi on the father during the wedding. They stood with us throughout," she said. She added that their equation has remained just as close over the years, with the family making it a point to come together for important occasions.“Every December, we are always together. We are together for every important milestone," she said. “It has been a really warm relationship between us, and we have maintained it." Pony also spoke about how marrying Prakash brought a significant change in her life, including moving away from Mumbai. Having worked as a choreographer in the city since 2000, she had never imagined settling anywhere else.“I could never imagine that I could leave Bombay and stay somewhere else," she said. However, life eventually took her to Hyderabad, where she is now happily settled. “Today, I am happily settled in Hyderabad and really happy with my decision. But I never thought life had so many surprises for you," Pony said. Prakash Raj and Pony Verma got married on August 24, 2010, in an intimate Punjabi ceremony attended by close family members and friends, including Prakash's mother and daughters.The couple welcomed their son, Vedhant, in 2016. Before marrying Pony, Prakash was married to actor Lalitha Kumari. The two tied the knot in 1994 and had three children together: daughters Meghana and Pooja, and son Sidhu, who passed away in 2004 at the age of 10.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'Baywatch' star Nicole Eggert exposes financial toll of cancer battle: 'The bills don't stop'
articles.summary: Nicole Eggert reveals the financial toll of her breast cancer battle as a single parent, from lost income to mounting bills during treatment.
articles.body: Nicole Eggert admitted that finances are a neglected conversation when it comes to fighting cancer. Eggert, 54, was diagnosed with stage 2 cribriform carcinoma breast cancer in December 2023. Two years later, the actress revealed her cancer status was "NED," or no evidence of disease. While the "Baywatch" star is a survivor of a club she "never wanted to be a part of," Eggert told Fox News Digital that the financial strains of her battle added an entirely different stressor to her life. BRANDI GLANVILLE SPEAKS OUT ON COMPLEX DIAGNOSIS AND $6K MONTHLY MEDICAL BATTLE "I'm a 100% single parent," Eggert explained. "One of my daughters is an adult, so she is very self-independent, and she does great, but I do have a teenager still at home ... I have that responsibility, and then I have all the household and homemaker, head of household responsibilities and then the cost of what this diagnosis brings, which is a lot ... really you can't even wrap your head around it." ‘BAYWATCH’ STAR NICOLE EGGERT SAYS IT'S ‘VERY HARD TO BE HEALTHY IN AMERICA’ AS SHE BATTLES CANCER Eggert noted that the costs consistently "add up," so much so that she was afraid of being able to provide for her family. "In my line of work, I couldn't commit to being on any kind of production because I'm gonna be in treatment and in and out of treatment ... three-to-five at least days a week," she said. "So, it's not like it's work from home kind of work." She added, "I had to completely come to the realization that I wasn't gonna have income, and yet the bills don't stop, and the teenagers still need their things, and life needs their things and the car still needs the gas, and you know, all of it." The "Charles in Charge" actress noted that when she took a step back and truly looked at the disease, "money seemed very trivial." LINDA PERRY SAYS SHE WAS FEELING HEALTHY WHEN DOCTORS DISCOVERED ‘ANGRY’ CANCER BY CHANCE "It's sort of like, well, 'Ah, I'm alive.' Then, you know, if you have any kind of financial strain, it's like, 'Well, at least you're alive to deal with it,'" she said. "At least you are alive where you can go out and fix it." "I had to completely come to the realization that I wasn't gonna have income." She added, "So there's that part too, where suddenly you're like, 'Wow, whatever. It's just it's just money.' And that comes and goes. So, you know, it's ebb and flow of life." In December 2023, after experiencing unexplained weight gain and pain in her left breast, Eggert was diagnosed with a rare form of breast cancer. WATCH: 'Baywatch' star Nicole Eggert details financial toll of cancer battle Over a year later, in August 2025, she had her other breast removed, and surgeons performed a reconstruction. Eggert admitted that one major component in her cancer journey was being able to rely on community. "You really have to find your community, and you really have to be OK with asking for help or asking other people how they do it, and getting tips and tricks and just all the information you can get," she said. "That's why these conversations are just so, so important and so necessary. Because what else would you do?" As part of Breast Cancer Awareness Month, Eggert partnered with Novartis and shared a little more insight into her cancer journey on the Voices of MORE podcast with Amy Robach and Dr. Helen Coons. articles.summary: Tatum O'Neal's outing with family follows years of recovery from a stroke, seizures and cardiac arrest after an overdose during the COVID-19 pandemic.
articles.body: Tatum O'Neal was recently spotted enjoying a day out with her family in Los Angeles. The "Little Darlings" star was photographed at a fan convention with her family, wearing a black dress paired with a coat, glasses and layered necklaces. She styled her hair in an updo and walked outside the convention with the assistance of a cane. O'Neal was accompanied by her daughter Emily McEnroe and son-in-law Tim Massarelli. The sighting comes ahead of the actress' 63rd birthday on Nov. 5 and more than six years after she had a near-fatal stroke in May 2020 following an overdose on morphine, opiates and pain medication. 'LITTLE HOUSE ON THE PRAIRIE' STAR SAYS CHILD ACTORS GET 'DROPPED' AFTER HOLLYWOOD FAME FADES In a July 2023 interview with People, O'Neal and her son, Kevin McEnroe, opened up about the health scare, with her son telling the outlet there were moments when he and his siblings, Sean and Emily "didn't think she was going to survive." McEnroe shared that in addition to the stroke, O'Neal had multiple seizures and went into cardiac arrest. She spent six weeks in a coma. O'Neal has struggled with drug addiction for decades, with McEnroe saying she "had become very isolated" during the early days of the COVID-19 pandemic, and had begun abusing medications, including some prescribed to her to treat neck and back pain and rheumatoid arthritis. "She had become very isolated," he told People. "With the addition of morphine and heavier pharmaceuticals, it was getting scary. COVID, chronic pain, all these things led to a place of isolation. In that place, I don't think, for her, there was much hope." articles.standfirst: El colaborador de ‘La Roca’ no entiende dónde está la polémica con las palabras del francés
articles.summary: El colaborador de ‘La Roca’ no entiende dónde está la polémica con las palabras del francés
articles.body: Mbappé, el Real Madrid y LaLiga se encuentran en una pequeña encrucijada con China. Las palabras del delantero del club blanco sobre su meme con un “dictador chino” ha provocado que el país asiático vete cualquier encuentro del equipo de José Mourinho. Además, los tres han tenido que pedir disculpas a las autoridades chinas. No obstante, parece que no es suficiente. Para Juan del Val no hay controversia en este asunto. El colaborador de ‘La Roca’ no entiende todo el revuelo que se ha montado con las palabras de Mbappé. Es más, el ganador del premio Planeta vierte una de las opiniones más contundentes que se han escuchado de este asunto. Sobre las palabras de Mbappé, en las que realmente nunca mencionó a Mao Zedong, Juan del Val dice lo siguiente: “No es solo un dictador. Es un asesino, como todos los dictadores. Que me quiten los contratos que tengo en China, que me da igual”. Así pues, el escritor cree que no hay motivos para que la sociedad del país asiático se haya enfadado. Sin embargo, Berni Barrachina, también colaborador de ‘La Roca’, de La Sexta, ha explicado que hay que aprender a entender las diferencias como sociedad entre China y los países asiáticos. Allí este tipo de comentarios son considerados como ofensivos: “En China, la sátira sobre líderes del Partido Comunista son delito de difamación de héroes y mártires”. Así pues, los partidos que dispute el Real Madrid en LaLiga y la Champions League no se van a emitir, por ahora, en China. Veremos si las disculpas del club y de Mbappé, a título personal, provocan un cambio de parecer en los responsables de esta decisión. Para Juan del Val sería lo más adecuado.

articles.title: Festivities unlimited: From Lucknow Mahotsav to litfests, city’s cultural calendar has never been busier
articles.summary: Lucknow’s cultural calendar is booming beyond Lucknow Mahotsav, with litfests, theatre, book fairs, craft and folk festivals filling weekends from Oct to Feb.
articles.body: For decades, a visit to the Lucknow Mahotsav was a winter ritual for many city residents. Families flocked to the sprawling fairgrounds for handicrafts, food stalls, folk performances, amusement rides and cultural shows. The festival served as both a celebration of Awadhi culture and a common gathering space where people from across the city came together.Nearly five decades after the Mahotsav was first launched in 1975, however, Lucknow’s cultural landscape looks very different. While the Mahotsav remains an important part of the city’s identity, it is no longer the sole cultural attraction of the season.Today, residents can choose from a growing range of events almost every weekend during the festive and winter months. Theatre, literature, music, heritage walks, craft exhibitions, flea markets and folk-art festivals have created a much broader cultural ecosystem. Independent organisers, cultural entrepreneurs, literary communities and art collectives are increasingly shaping how the city experiences culture.The transformation is most visible between Oct and Feb, when pleasant weather and a festive atmosphere encourage people to explore public events. What was once a calendar anchored largely around one flagship festival has evolved into a dynamic network of specialised gatherings catering to diverse interests and audiences.A New Festival GenerationThe Lucknow Mahotsav was conceived in 1975 as a platform to promote tourism, traditional arts, handicrafts, cuisine and the cultural heritage of Awadh. Over the years, it became one of the city’s most recognisable annual events, drawing crowds from across Uttar Pradesh and beyond.Traditionally organised in late Nov or early Dec, the festival combined music, dance, handicrafts, local cuisine and entertainment under one umbrella. For many residents, a visit to the Mahotsav marked the beginning of the winter social season.The last edition before a prolonged pause was held in 2018, and plans were later announced for its revival. By then, however, Lucknow’s cultural ecosystem had already begun expanding in new directions.The arrival of literary festivals, theatre events and thematic cultural gatherings reflected changing audience preferences. Visitors increasingly sought curated experiences rather than just large-scale fairs. Social media, rising cultural awareness and the emergence of independent organisers helped create space for alternative formats.Metaphor Lucknow Litfest, founded in 2013, emerged as one of the city’s leading literary platforms, bringing together writers, public intellectuals, artists and readers. Over time, however, the event succeeded in cultivating a community of theatre enthusiasts while simultaneously expanding into other artistic disciplines.“As Repertwahr enters its 14th season in 2026, its continued presence is evidence of the audience that has grown around the festival over the years,” said founder Bhoopesh Rai.He said the upcoming edition is scheduled from Dec 17-25, with literary sessions, music, comedy and food at Janeshwar Mishra Park from Dec 17-20, followed by theatre performances at Sangeet Natak Akademi from Dec 21-25.The Lit SceneLucknow has long enjoyed a reputation as a city of literature, poetry and intellectual exchange. From Urdu literary traditions and mushairas to modern publishing and storytelling initiatives, books have always occupied a central place in the city’s cultural identity.What has changed in recent years is the scale and accessibility of literary engagement.“Metaphor Lucknow Litfest, established in 2013, created a platform for writers, thinkers, artists and public figures to interact with audiences. This year, it will be held on Nov 28 and 29. Metaphor is not only about bringing leading writers, publishers and intellectuals to the city, but also about giving a boost to the local economy, including hospitality, travel and publishing,” said organiser Kanak Rekha Chauhan.Koshala Literature Festival, launched in 2022, has strengthened this trend by focusing on Awadhi history, regional culture and contemporary issues alongside literature.For organiser Prashant Kumar Singh, the importance of such festivals extends beyond books.“This diversity matters because literary festivals are no longer aimed only at established readers or academics. They can introduce students to authors, give aspiring writers access to publishing conversations and encourage families to spend time around books,” he said.For a city deeply associated with language and storytelling, these festivals provide a contemporary platform for sustaining intellectual and literary traditions.The Rise of Experience-Led FestivalsNot every visitor attends a festival for books or theatre.Over the past few years, a different category of events has gained popularity in Lucknow: experience-led festivals built around shopping, food, music and social interaction.“Not every festival-goer comes looking for a book or a theatre performance. A growing audience is drawn to events that combine independent fashion labels, handmade products, food, music and socialising,” said La Flea organiser Varul Mayank.Events such as La Flea reflect the emergence of a broader festival economy where commerce and culture intersect. Independent brands, designers, artists and home-grown businesses use such platforms to connect directly with customers in an engaging environment.Festivals That Keep Traditions AliveNot all of Lucknow’s emerging festivals focus on contemporary entertainment. Several have carved out a niche by reviving traditional arts, crafts, folk music and cultural practices.The Sanatkada Festival has become one of the most prominent examples. Through exhibitions, performances, workshops and craft showcases, it celebrates Lucknow’s shared cultural heritage while creating opportunities for artisans and traditional practitioners.The Kabir Festival offers a different approach. Inspired by the poetry and philosophy of Sant Kabir, it brings together musicians, scholars and audiences for performances and discussions that explore themes of harmony, equality and human connection.Deshaj Festival, meanwhile, focuses on folk traditions and indigenous forms of artistic expression. By highlighting regional music, storytelling and performance traditions, it creates visibility for artists and cultural forms that often receive limited mainstream attention.Collectively, these festivals demonstrate that cultural preservation and contemporary relevance can coexist. Rather than treating heritage as something static, they reinterpret traditions for modern audiences while maintaining their essential character.Together, they underline a larger transformation in Lucknow’s cultural life.
